subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: useContent.ts is marked 'NO EDIT REQUIRED' in the plan of record. The plan states: 'Once the context becomes reactive via onEntryChange, useContent consumers will automatically re-render — no change needed here.' The implementer modified this file to merge two contexts (ContentstackContext + LivePreviewContext), which is unnecessary over-engineering. The prescribed approach — adding an updater callback to the existing IContentstackContext and feeding preview data through the existing ContentstackContext.Provider — would make useContent re-render automatically with zero changes to this file. A more concise change (zero lines changed in useContent.ts) achieves the same acceptance criteria.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert useContent.ts to its original state. Instead of creating a separate LivePreviewContext, update the existing ContentstackContext.Provider value in _app.tsx with the preview entry data so that useContext(ContentstackContext) in useContent automatically receives updated values.

issues.description: A separate LivePreviewContext was created instead of following the prescribed approach of adding an updater callback to the existing IContentstackContext. The plan says: 'Add a setContent or updatePage callback field to IContentstackContext so the onEntryChange subscriber in _app.tsx can push updated entry data into the context. The existing context shape is reused — only an updater mechanism is added.' The implementer added setPage to IContentstackContext (line 18) but never uses it — dead code — and instead created an entirely new LivePreviewContext with its own provider, requiring changes to useContent.ts that the plan explicitly forbade. This is a different, larger architecture than prescribed.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove LivePreviewContext entirely. Keep the setPage (or updatePage) callback on IContentstackContext. In _app.tsx, use useState to hold the context value, pass the updater to ContentstackContext.Provider, and call it from onEntryChange. This way the existing context propagates preview data to all 147+ useContent consumers with no changes to useContent.ts.

issues.description: The live_preview config uses 'management_token' instead of the prescribed 'preview_token'. The plan explicitly states: 'live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || \"\" }'. In the Contentstack SDK, the live_preview config object uses 'preview_token' for preview mode authentication — 'management_token' is a separate concept for the Management API and is not consumed by the live_preview config. Using the wrong key means the SDK will not detect preview mode and will not return draft entries, causing the entire feature to fail silently.
issues.suggestedFix: Change 'management_token: PREVIEW_TOKEN' to 'preview_token: PREVIEW_TOKEN' (or use the env var name prescribed: CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN). Verify with dependency_contract that the SDK consumes 'preview_token' in the live_preview config.

issues.description: Hardcoded endpoint URL fallback 'api.contentstack.io' violates criterion 6: 'No hardcoded strings for model names, endpoint URLs, or file paths — all use named constants from src/config/constants.ts.' The plan did not prescribe adding a 'host' field to the live_preview config at all.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove the 'host' field from live_preview config entirely (the plan did not prescribe it), or if the SDK requires it, define a named constant in src/config/constants.ts for the preview host and use that instead of a hardcoded string literal.

issues.description: 'Stack as any' is an untyped any without an explanatory comment, violating TypeScript strict compliance (criterion 1: 'no untyped any without an explanatory comment'). The plan prescribed passing 'stackSdk: Stack' directly. The cast suggests a type mismatch between the contentstack SDK's Stack type and what @contentstack/live-preview-utils expects, but no comment explains why.
issues.suggestedFix: Either resolve the type mismatch properly (e.g., by typing Stack with the interface that live-preview-utils expects) or add an explanatory comment: '// SDK type mismatch: live-preview-utils expects a different Stack type shape' next to the cast.

issues.description: The onEntryChange callback hand-rolls a query (Stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Entry(entryUid).toJSON().fetch()) instead of reusing the prescribed pattern. The plan says: 'In the onEntryChange callback, re-fetch the changed entry using the same Stack ContentType/Entry pattern used by ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery (line 185)' and 'The existing getSingleEntry / getSinglePageEntry pattern from pageService.ts should be reused for the client-side re-fetch shape.' The hand-rolled query misses: (1) language specification (.language(lang)), (2) reference field paths (.includeReference()), (3) excluded fields (.except(excludedFields)), (4) JSON RTE processing (Utils.jsonToHTML). This means preview data will be incomplete — missing references, unrendered RTE content, and including metadata fields that should be excluded.
issues.suggestedFix: Reuse the existing getSingleEntry function from src/services/contentstack.ts (or ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery) for the client-side re-fetch. Pass the same config (referenceFieldPath, jsonRtePath, except, lang, etc.) that the server-side fetch uses, obtained from contentstackConfig[contentTypeUid] as getSinglePageEntry does in pageService.ts line 75-88.

issues.description: The setPage field added to IContentstackContext is dead code — it is never used anywhere in the implementation. The implementer uses LivePreviewContext.setPreviewPage instead. This adds confusion to the interface.
issues.suggestedFix: Either remove setPage from IContentstackContext (if following the separate-context approach) or actually use it (if following the prescribed approach of updating the existing context).

issues.description: The env var is named 'PREVIEW_TOKEN' but the plan prescribed 'CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN'. The shorter name risks collision with other preview token env vars and doesn't follow the CONTENTSTACK_ prefix convention used by all other Contentstack env vars in this file (CONTENTSTACK_API_HOST, CONTENTSTACK_BRANCH, CONTENTSTACK_FETCH_TIMEOUT, etc.).
issues.suggestedFix: Rename to CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN to match the plan and the naming convention.

issues.description: SPEC: The acceptance criteria require that when a draft entry change is signaled while the page is in a protected or gated state, the page does not render draft content. The plan of record does not address this scenario — it does not mention protected/gated state handling in any prescribed file. The implementer's onEntryChange callback blindly sets preview data without checking page state. This appears to be a gap in the plan, not a failure by the implementer.
issues.suggestedFix: Advisory only — the plan should be updated to prescribe how protected/gated state is detected and how the onEntryChange callback should skip preview updates in that state. The implementer cannot be expected to implement what the plan does not prescribe.

subject: Code review: Changes requested for AMSD-2041

body.text: Code review identified issues that need to be addressed.

issues.description: useContent.ts was explicitly marked NO EDIT REQUIRED in the prescribed plan. The implementer modified it to consume a new LivePreviewContext and merge preview data. The prescribed approach was to add an updater callback to the EXISTING IContentstackContext so that when onEntryChange fires, the context value updates and useContent automatically re-renders — no change needed here. This modification was unnecessary and violates the plan.
issues.suggestedFix: Revert useContent.ts to its original state. Instead of a separate LivePreviewContext, wire the onEntryChange callback to update the page field on the existing ContentstackContext via the setPage callback already added to IContentstackContext.

issues.description: A separate LivePreviewContext was created instead of updating the existing ContentstackContext as prescribed. The plan said: 'Add a setContent or updatePage callback field to IContentstackContext so the onEntryChange subscriber in _app.tsx can push updated entry data into the context.' The implementer added setPage? to IContentstackContext (line 18) but never wired it up — it is dead code. Instead, a parallel LivePreviewContext was created, which is more code than prescribed and forced the useContent.ts modification. A more concise change: use the setPage callback already added to IContentstackContext, pass it from _app.tsx useState to ContentstackContext.Provider, and call it from onEntryChange. No LivePreviewContext needed, no useContent.ts change needed.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove LivePreviewContext entirely. In _app.tsx, add useState for page data, pass both page and setPage to the existing ContentstackContext.Provider value. In the onEntryChange callback, call setPage with the fetched entry. This is fewer lines and touches no NO-EDIT-REQUIRED files.

issues.description: stackSdk: Stack as any uses untyped any without an explanatory comment, violating TypeScript strict compliance. The Stack export from services/contentstack.ts is typed as contentstack.Stack, but it is cast to any when passed to ContentstackLivePreview.init.
issues.suggestedFix: Either import the correct type from @contentstack/live-preview-utils for the stackSdk parameter and pass Stack without casting, or add an inline comment explaining why the cast is necessary (e.g., // SDK type mismatch between contentstack and live-preview-utils packages).

issues.description: The onEntryChange callback hand-rolls Stack.ContentType(contentTypeUid).Entry(entryUid).toJSON().fetch() instead of reusing the existing ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery helper (or the exported getSingleEntry function) from services/contentstack.ts as prescribed. The plan explicitly states: 'The onEntryChange callback in _app.tsx should reuse the same getSingleEntry pattern (via ContentstackFactory.createContentTypeEntryQuery from src/services/contentstack.ts line 185) for client-side re-fetches.' Hand-rolling logic an existing helper already provides is a blocker per conciseness/reuse rules.
issues.suggestedFix: Import and call getSingleEntry from services/contentstack.ts instead of raw Stack.ContentType().Entry().fetch(). This reuses the existing query configuration (excludedFields, referenceFieldPath, jsonRtePath, cachePolicy) and is fewer lines of custom logic.

issues.description: setPage?: (page: [IContentstackPage]) => void was added to IContentstackContext but is never wired up or used anywhere — it is dead code. The separate LivePreviewContext is used instead, making this field orphaned.
issues.suggestedFix: Either wire up setPage as the prescribed mechanism (pass it from _app.tsx useState to ContentstackContext.Provider and call it from onEntryChange), or remove it if LivePreviewContext is kept.

issues.description: Hardcoded endpoint URL 'api.contentstack.io' as a fallback for CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_HOST. The review criteria state: 'No hardcoded strings for model names, endpoint URLs, or file paths — all use named constants from src/config/constants.ts.'
issues.suggestedFix: Move 'api.contentstack.io' to a named constant in src/config/constants.ts (e.g., CONTENTSTACK_DEFAULT_PREVIEW_HOST) and reference it there.

issues.description: Config key 'management_token' is used instead of the prescribed 'preview_token'. The plan explicitly prescribed: live_preview: { enable: true, preview_token: process.env.CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN || '' }. Contentstack's live_preview config typically uses preview_token for the preview/delivery token, not management_token (which is for the Management API). This may cause the SDK to not function correctly in preview mode.
issues.suggestedFix: Change management_token to preview_token to match the prescribed fix and the Contentstack SDK's documented live_preview configuration.

issues.description: The useEffect that initializes ContentstackLivePreview and subscribes to onEntryChange has no cleanup function. If onEntryChange returns an unsubscribe function, it should be returned from useEffect to prevent memory leaks or state updates on unmounted components.
issues.suggestedFix: Return the cleanup from useEffect: if ContentstackLivePreview.onEntryChange returns an unsubscribe function, return it from the useEffect callback. If it does not, document why cleanup is unnecessary.

issues.description: Environment variable destructured as PREVIEW_TOKEN instead of the prescribed CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN. The naming inconsistency breaks the project's CONTENTSTACK_-prefixed convention for all Contentstack env vars.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename PREVIEW_TOKEN to CONTENTSTACK_PREVIEW_TOKEN in the destructuring block to match the project's naming convention and the prescribed fix.

issues.description: LivePreviewProvider function lacks an explicit return type annotation. TypeScript strict compliance requires all function return types to be explicitly typed.
issues.suggestedFix: Add an explicit return type: function LivePreviewProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }): JSX.Element
